questions.question: Describe the depth–time graph of a bath that fills steadily, is used, then drains steadily, using the words linear, increasing, constant and decreasing.
questions.expected_answer: Linear and increasing while filling (steady tap), constant while in use (depth unchanged), linear and decreasing while draining. Three straight pieces: rising, level, falling.

questions.question: What is the difference between a linear and a non-linear graph, with an example of each?
questions.expected_answer: Linear is a straight line: the quantity changes by the same amount each unit of time, as for a car at steady speed. Non-linear curves: the rate changes, as for a kettle heating quickly then slowly.

questions.question: Why does a horizontal part of a distance–time graph not mean the person went back home?
questions.expected_answer: Horizontal means the distance is not changing: the person has stopped. Going back home would make the distance decrease, shown by a falling line.
